title: Designing Idempotent .NET APIs for Enterprise Integrations
excerpt: Patterns for safe retries, outbox messaging, and reconciliation when integrating ERP and Dynamics 365 workloads.
content:
# Designing Idempotent .NET APIs for Enterprise Integrations

Enterprise integrations fail in the real world — networks drop, partners retry, and partial commits happen. Idempotency is how you survive that reality.

## Why it matters
When a Dynamics 365 or ERP client retries a POST, you must not create duplicate invoices or stock movements.

## Practical approach
1. Accept a client-generated `Idempotency-Key`
2. Persist request fingerprints in an integration store
3. Use an outbox for reliable downstream publish
4. Expose reconciliation reports for finance

## Takeaway
Treat idempotency as a product requirement, not an afterthought.
author: Muhammad Babar Ali

title: SQL Server Indexing Strategies for Heavy ERP Reports
excerpt: How covering indexes, indexed views, and curated marts turn 45-second reports into interactive ones.
content:
# SQL Server Indexing Strategies for Heavy ERP Reports

Reporting is often the silent performance killer in ERP systems.

## Patterns that work
- Separate OLTP from reporting schemas
- Use indexed views for stable aggregates
- Prefer covering indexes for filter + include columns used by SSRS
- Schedule heavy packs asynchronously

## Result
Teams stop fearing month-end because reports become predictable.
author: Muhammad Babar Ali

title: Clean Architecture for Modular ERP Systems
excerpt: Bounding contexts for inventory, production, and finance without drowning in ceremony.
content:
# Clean Architecture for Modular ERP Systems

ERP systems grow until boundaries blur. Clean Architecture helps — if applied pragmatically.

## Guidance
- Align modules with business capabilities
- Keep domain logic free of UI and infrastructure
- Allow pragmatic shared kernels for cross-cutting concerns

Architecture should accelerate delivery, not slow it down.
author: Muhammad Babar Ali
